integration.name: Resend
integration.tagline: One key, and a webhook that tells you what happened
integration.summary: A developer-first mail API. The connection needs a single key, and the provider reports delivery and inbound mail back over a signed webhook — which is the only email path where the console can show you what happened after acceptance.

credentials.label: API Key
credentials.note: From the Resend dashboard. A sending-scoped key is enough.

credentials.label: Webhook signing secret
credentials.note: Only needed if you want inbound replies and delivery events to reach the console. Find it under Webhooks → that endpoint → signing secret.

config.label: Sender address (From)
config.note: The address your mail goes out as. It must sit on a domain verified in your Resend account.

strengths: A single API key to connect
Signed webhooks, so inbound mail is verified rather than trusted
Delivery events normalized into the same statuses as SMS
Domain verification stays in your own Resend account
considerations: You provide the From address as part of the connection, not per send — every send on this connection goes out as that address.
Without the webhook signing secret the console rejects inbound events, so replies and delivery updates never appear.
